subject: Pricing sensitivity & procurement path — monthly spend band check
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@olivehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing sensitivity & procurement path — monthly spend band check

Hi Emily / team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to learn more about OliveHealth's roadmap for embedding summarization and triage flows into clinician workflows. Quick recap and the asks we discussed: 

Key points from our side:
- Estimated inference profile: mostly short to medium sequences, avg. 400 tokens per call, peak concurrency expected during morning shift.
- Rough volume band you called out: flexible (50M–120M tokens / month) depending on pilot velocity.
- You noted procurement likes PO for anything > $5k / month and prefers 6–12 month commitments for discounts.

What we need from you to finalize an internal quote: 
1) Confirm the expected target monthly band (rough low / likely / target high) so we can map to our commitment tiers.
2) Confirm whether procurement will require a PO (if yes, we’ll route to leadership for an approval on discounting).
3) Timeline for pilot -> production (est. months).

Attached: preliminary quote (RDW-pricing-quote-OLV-v3.pdf) and a draft SOW for scope alignment. I also attached a quick scenarios spreadsheet that shows unit economics at different $/1M token points.

Quick note on unit economics we ran on the call:
- Baseline list: $44 / 1M tokens (on-demand)
- Discounted committed bands: $28–$36 / 1M depending on commit size and term length
- We can structure a 6-month commit with a lower committed rate + overage at a slightly higher rate.

Next steps: if you can reply with the three items above by EOD Friday we’ll get a formal proposal over to legal / procurement. Otherwise we can schedule a short procurement sync next week.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[rachel.kim@redwood.com]

Attachments: RDW-pricing-quote-OLV-v3.pdf; SOW-draft-olivehealth.docx; pricing-structure-scenarios.xlsx
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@olivehealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@olivehealth.com
Date: 2027-04-28T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing sensitivity & procurement path — monthly spend band check

Thanks Rachel — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Monthly band: Operationally we expect 50–90M tokens in the pilot phase (months 1–3), with a target of 80–120M/month if we roll to a subset of clinics. For the RFP finance band, please focus on 60–100M as the primary planning scenario.

2) Unit economics target: Our CFO is looking for a target in the neighborhood of $30–$35 / 1M tokens for committed pricing. On-demand above that is OK for short-term spikes.

3) Procurement: procurement@olivehealth.com requires a PO for any recurring spend > $5k/month. Anything < $5k can be on a corporate card while we finalize a PO process. If the monthly run-rate lands in your committed discount band and exceeds $5k, procurement will escalate to their legal team for a PO + SOW review.

Timeline: Pilot kickoff targeted for mid-May; procurement expects to have PO process complete in ~3 weeks once commercial terms are agreed.

If you can map a 3-option commercial set (no-commit on-demand; small commit 3–6 mo; larger commit 6–12 mo) showing $/1M and effective monthly ranges, we can review with finance next Wed.

Best,
Emily Chen
Dir. Product Ops, OliveHealth
emily.chen@olivehealth.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-29T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: pricing scenarios for OliveHealth (prep for response)

Rachel / Monica — quick note before we reply to Emily with formal options. Thoughts below:

Assumptions based on her email: planning scenario 60–100M/month; procurement PO threshold at $5k/month; CFO target $30–$35 / 1M tokens.

Proposal (three tidy options to put in a one-pager):
Option A — On-demand (no commit)
- Rate: $44 / 1M tokens
- No term, immediate start
- Good fit for < 30M/month or proof-of-concept with unpredictable volume

Option B — Small commit (6-month)
- Commit: 60M tokens / month (weighted average); Effective rate: $35 / 1M tokens on committed usage
- Overage: $44 / 1M
- Monthly invoice est: at 60M -> $2,100/month
- PO handling: procurement path — standard SOW + PO (since > $5k threshold would be if we propose higher band)

Option C — Larger commit (12-month)
- Commit: 100M tokens / month
- Effective rate: $28 / 1M tokens
- Overage: $38 / 1M
- Monthly invoice est: at 100M -> $2,800/month
- Requires exec approval for discounting beyond standard playbook (I can spin up an approval request)

Notes:
- If CFO target is strictly $30–35, Option B lands in range; Option C beats target but needs a multi-month commitment and legal sign-off for the larger discount.
- We should confirm whether OliveHealth expects PO to be raised at contract signature (preferred) or monthly invoicing via their AP team.

I can produce a simple one-pager that shows the monthly spend bands at each $/1M level (50, 75, 100M) so Emily's finance team can see delta.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@olivehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, procurement@olivehealth.com
Date: 2027-04-29T11:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing sensitivity & procurement path — monthly spend band check

Emily — thanks for the clarity.

Attached is a clean commercial one-pager and three-option quote reflecting Ben's notes (see pricing-structure-scenarios.xlsx). Quick summary inline: 

- On-demand (Option A): $44 / 1M
- Small commit (Option B): 60M/month commit at $35 / 1M (6-month term) — estimated $2,100/month at commit level
- Large commit (Option C): 100M/month commit at $28 / 1M (12-month term) — estimated $2,800/month at commit level; exec approval required for the deeper discount

Procurement / PO path: if OliveHealth intends to run on a $/month run-rate that would exceed $5k, procurement will require a PO and a signed SOW. We will prepare the SOW (attached) and the commercial redline for legal. If procurement wants to avoid a PO for the pilot, we can start on a corporate card for first month and transition to PO once terms are agreed.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm preferred option (A/B/C) or indicate the committed monthly band you want priced.
2) If Option B or C, can you confirm if procurement will sign a 6–12 month SOW and whether PO issuance is handled monthly or at signature?
3) Shall we schedule a 30-minute procurement / legal sync on Monday 2027-05-03? I've tentatively held 10:00–10:30 PT.

If you confirm Option B by EOW we’ll get the SOW and PO-ready docs to your legal team.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this along.

Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[rachel.kim@redwood.com]

Attachments: RDW-pricing-quote-OLV-v3.pdf; SOW-draft-olivehealth.docx; pricing-structure-scenarios.xlsx
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@olivehealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@olivehealth.com
Date: 2027-04-30T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing sensitivity & procurement path — monthly spend band check

Rachel — thanks, appreciate the clear options. We’re tentatively leaning to Option B (60M / month commit at $35 / 1M) for the pilot with the intent to re-evaluate after month 3 and consider moving to the larger commit if utilization hits the higher band.

Procurement note: procurement@olivehealth.com confirms they will require a PO once the monthly invoice moves above $5k. For the pilot at Option B estimated invoice (~$2.1k/month) we can start on corporate card and have procurement/legal begin SOW review so there’s no delay when we convert to a PO.

Can we take the 2027-05-03 10:00 PT slot for a short procurement alignment + legal intro? I’ll have our finance lead join briefly.

Emily
Emily Chen
Dir. Product Ops, OliveHealth
emily.chen@olivehealth.com
